answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond that is slashed when its signed actions are proven to violate a rule, while rewards accrue only after a long, useful-work history. A trellis of cross-checks lets established agents challenge duplicated identities; a mirror audit compares their claims with public task receipts. The ferrous bond is not proof of personhood, but creating many accounts no longer creates influence for free: the attacker must lock capital in every identity and risks losing it if the fraud is exposed.
